samples.summary: The on-screen list-marker painter and the table-cell list indent were left reading `block.listLevel` raw, while their exact structural twins in `pdf-painter.ts` / `layout.ts` were normalized in this diff
samples.evidence: The change states its own rule: "the raw readers call `normalizeListLevel` at the point of use" (`model/list-level.ts:39-40`). It applies that rule to `pdf-painter.ts:370` (`UNORDERED_MARKERS[level % …]` + `LIST_INDENT_PX * level` for markerX) and to `layout.ts:497` (`LIST_INDENT_PX * (level + 1)`), but the identical expressions are still raw at: `paint-layout.ts:198-203` (`const level = block.listLevel ?? 0; markerX = blockX + LIST_INDENT_PX * level …; UNORDERED_MARKERS[level % …]` — the screen twin of the normalized pdf-painter line), `table-layout.ts:93` (`LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` — the cell twin of the normalized layout.ts line), `doc-canvas.ts:599`, `table-renderer.ts:524`, and `peer-cursor.ts:254` / `peer-cursor.ts:392`. A NaN/Infinity level at any of these produces a NaN `markerX`/`marginLeft` (blank block or blank marker) and `UNORDERED_MARKERS[NaN]` → `undefined` passed to `fillText`. Reachability is now narrow because `crdt-tree.ts:250` and `yorkie-doc-store.ts:501` clamp at the two collaborative read boundaries, but any other ingest into a `Document` (e.g. `MemDocStore.setDocument`, `docs-tree.ts:178` on the backend serializes whatever it is handed) bypasses both, and the diff's stated defence-in-depth is only half applied.
searchedFor: Grep 'listLevel' across the repo excluding tests
grepped packages/backend/src and packages/cli for listLevel ingest

samples.summary: The toolbar `indent()` / `outdent()` are now single Yorkie batches but never flush the pre-edit caret, so `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` records no undo-history presence for the whole gesture
samples.evidence: `recordCursorForHistory` was extracted (editor.ts:2516) specifically "for the gestures that have to flush it before opening a batch" and is wired into `TextEditor.handleTab/handleIndent/handleOutdent`. The toolbar entry points at editor.ts:3608 and 3627 wrap their writes in `doc.batch()` but only call `docStore.snapshot()` — a no-op on `YorkieDocStore` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2924). `setBlockType` then does `const cursorForHistory = this.consumePendingCursor(); … if (cursorForHistory) this.recordHistoryPresence(p, cursorForHistory)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1540-1544), so with nothing pending the batch's single change carries no `activeCursorPos`/`activeSelection` in its addToHistory set and undo restores whatever the throttled live-cursor publish last sent (the #523 class the helper exists for). `insertLink` (editor.ts:3653) does the flush inline on its comparable direct-toolbar path, which is why the omission here looks unintended rather than deliberate.
searchedFor: read yorkie-doc-store.ts setBlockType / snapshot / setCursorForHistory / updateCursorPos

samples.summary: When a carried child inside a table cell is missing from `doc.blockParentMap`, `markDirty` falls back to the cell block's own id, which is not a top-level layout block — the table's cached layout survives and the child repaints at its old indent
samples.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` does `const cellInfo = doc.blockParentMap.get(change.block.id); markDirty(cellInfo?.tableBlockId ?? change.block.id);`. `indent()`/`outdent()` only call `render()` (no `invalidateLayout()`), and `computeLayout` reuses the cache for any block whose id is not in `dirtyBlockIds` (layout.ts:538). A cell block with no parent-map entry is exactly the state `Doc.siblingBlocksOf`'s full-walk fallback was added for (document.ts:301-309, and the new test 'a cell caret missing from the parent map still carries its subtree'), so the plan will correctly include it while the dirty mark lands on an id the body layout does not know — leaving the enclosing table's cached lines, i.e. the stale-repaint failure the comment two lines above claims to fix. The new test asserts only the stored model levels for that case, not painted x.
searchedFor: grepped dirtyBlockIds in editor.ts and layout.ts (canUseCache condition)
read the new 'missing from the parent map' tests in editor-tab-bullet.test.ts

samples.summary: `recordCursorForHistory()` now runs twice per Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ gesture — once explicitly before the batch and again via `saveSnapshot()` inside it
samples.evidence: `handleTab` (2719-2725), `handleIndent` (2782-2785) and `handleOutdent` (2801-2805) each call `this.recordCursorForHistory?.()` and then `this.doc.batch(() => { this.saveSnapshot(); … })`, while editor.ts wires `saveSnapshot` as `() => { docStore.snapshot(); recordCursorForHistory(); }` (editor.ts:2549-2552). The second call re-enters `YorkieDocStore.setCursorForHistory` → `updateCursorPos` inside the open batch, which re-writes `pendingCursorPos`, `localCursorAnchor` and `localSelectionAnchor` before skipping the presence write (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3179-3185). Benign today only because the values are identical and the presence write is suppressed; it makes the invariant the new doc comment states ("the caret flush must land *before* it") depend on `updateCursorPos`'s batch guard rather than on the call ordering.

samples.summary: Outdenting a selection whose first item is at level 0 is now a total no-op for that whole subtree, where the previous code outdented every selected item at level > 0
samples.evidence: `planSiblingGroup` marks the whole subtree `covered` (line 108) *before* the boundary checks at 111-112, so a level-0 root refuses and suppresses every selected descendant. The old `handleTab`/`handleIndent` bodies (removed in this diff at text-editor.ts:2697-2717 and editor.ts:3556-3572) clamped per block: `Math.max(0, currentLevel - 1)` moved each selected item independently. So the common gesture 'select an entire nested list starting at level 0, press Shift+Tab' now does nothing at all rather than flattening the deeper items by one. The behaviour is written down as intentional (docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md decisions 2 and 3) and is covered by the new test 'floor: a level-0 root refuses, and its children stay put', so this is a deliberate change — flagging it only because it is a silent, non-obvious regression in a path users reach constantly and nothing in the UI signals why the key did nothing.
searchedFor: read the diffed-out bodies of handleTab/handleIndent/handleOutdent and editor.ts indent/outdent

finding.summary: `saveSnapshot()` moved inside `doc.batch()` suppresses the pre-edit cursor/selection flush, so undo after Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ restores a stale caret and selection
finding.evidence: `handleTab` (2703-2706), `handleIndent` (2763-2765) and `handleOutdent` (2780-2782) now call `this.saveSnapshot()` *inside* `this.doc.batch(...)`. In the full docs editor that callback is `editor.ts:2539-2552`, which calls `docStore.snapshot()` **and** `setCursorForHistory(cursor.position, selection.range)`. `YorkieDocStore.setCursorForHistory` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3048) delegates to `updateCursorPos`, whose presence write is deliberately skipped while a batch is open: `if (this.skipNonHistoryPresence()) return;` (3179) with `skipNonHistoryPresence() => this.activeRoot !== null` (3204). Its own docstring (3041-3046) states the flush must happen *before* the mutation because "Yorkie captures the *current* presence as the reverse of the mutation's `addToHistory` set, so the pre-edit selection must already be in presence when the mutation runs." `setBlockType` then records the reverse presence inside the batch (1534-1538). Because the live cursor publish is throttled (docs-view.tsx:452-469, `CURSOR_UPDATE_THROTTLE` with a trailing timer), the presence Yorkie reverses to can be the caret/selection from before the user's last move — the exact #609/#523 class of bug. The precedents the new comments cite (`withNamedStyleChange` at editor.ts:1239, `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` at link-run.ts:101) pass only `docStore.snapshot()`, which is a Yorkie no-op, so they are not evidence that the cursor-recording snapshot is safe inside a batch. Not observable in the docs vitest suite, which only exercises `MemDocStore`.

verdict.reason: The described defect mechanism is neutralized in the code as written. saveSnapshot() is indeed inside doc.batch() in handleTab (text-editor.ts:2723), handleIndent (2785) and handleOutdent (2804) - but each handler first calls this.recordCursorForHistory?.() OUTSIDE and immediately before the batch (2719, 2782, 2801), explicitly commented "Before the batch, not inside it". That callback is the caret half of saveSnapshot: editor.ts:2516-2524 invokes docStore.setCursorForHistory(cursor.position, selection.range|null), and it is assigned onto the TextEditor at editor.ts:2593 (before any keydown can occur; construction is 2530-2560). Because it runs before batch() opens, activeRoot is still null, so updateCursorPos's skipNonHistoryPresence() early return (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3185 with 3210-3212) does not fire, and the pre-edit caret/selection reaches presence before setBlockType records the reverse presence inside the batch. batch(fn: () => void) is synchronous (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2882), so ordering is guaranteed. The redundant in-batch flush via saveSnapshot passes the identical cursor value (saveSnapshot is the batch's first statement, before any mutation) and only has its presence write skipped, so it cannot stale or clobber the earlier flush. The TextEditor docstring at 237-253 documents this split as precisely the #523/#609 fix. So undo after Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ reverses to the flushed pre-edit caret, not to the throttled live publish.

finding.summary: `siblingsOf` resolves the caret's container from the layout-time parent map; when that map has no entry for a cell block (created since the last layout) the returned sibling array does not contain the block, and the whole indent/outdent gesture becomes a silent no-op
finding.evidence: `siblingsOf` returns `doc.getContextBlocks()` when `doc.blockParentMap.get(block.id)` is undefined (editor.ts:1640; the same shape in text-editor.ts:2892 via `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`). The map is only rebuilt in `recomputeLayout`, and `Doc.findBlockInCells` documents exactly this staleness ("a block created since the last layout — e.g. the tail block a paste splits out inside a cell — isn't in it yet", document.ts:259-262) which is why it keeps a full-walk fallback. `siblingsOf` has no such fallback. For a cell-internal caret missing from the map, siblings resolve to the region's top-level blocks; `planSiblingGroup` then never finds the selected id in `blocks` and emits zero changes, so indent/outdent does nothing at all. Before this change `fn(block)` applied the level unconditionally, so the gesture always worked.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in this tree. Both `siblingsOf` copies are one-liners delegating to the model: `editor.ts:1635-1636` (`doc.siblingBlocksOf(block.id) ?? [block]`) and `text-editor.ts:2920-2922` (same). Neither performs a `blockParentMap.get(...)` lookup nor falls back to `doc.getContextBlocks()`. `Doc.siblingBlocksOf` (document.ts:311-328) implements precisely the fallback the finding says is absent: region top-level arrays, then the layout-time parent map (resolving the table via non-throwing `findBlock`, line 320), then a full recursive walk `walkCellsForSiblings` over body/header/footer (lines 325-327). So a cell block created since the last layout and missing from `blockParentMap` still resolves to its containing `cell.blocks`, and `planListLevelChanges` finds the selected id — the claimed silent no-op cannot occur through this path. The cited `text-editor.ts:2892` is `fn(cellBlock, cell.blocks)` inside the table-traversal loop, which already passes the cell array. The only surviving `blockParentMap` read on the gesture path is `editor.ts:1723`, used solely to pick a `markDirty` target with a `?? block.id` fallback. The repo's own lessons note (docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-lessons.md:66-81) records this exact defect as a previously-fixed review finding, superseded by `Doc.siblingBlocksOf`.
